code.text: He has coughed for about three months, now with streaks of blood, sweats at night, and has lost weight; he wants to know what is wrong
He teaches piano at home and performs; he wants to know when he can teach again and whether his students are at risk
He is afraid his students and neighbors will shun him if they learn he may have tuberculosis

dosageInstruction.text: 400 mg once daily with the other drugs by video-observed therapy with the health department, seven days a week, for 17 weeks; no mineral supplements within 4 hours before or 8 hours after

medicationCodeableConcept.text: Isoniazid 300 mg tablet, one tablet daily

text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Infectious diseases consultation to confirm the diagnosis, choose between the six-month and four-month regimens, plan monitoring and his return to teaching, and address cystic fibrosis and alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency as explanations for his lifelong chest illness
  • Diagnosis: three sputum samples at least eight hours apart, one early in the morning, for acid-fast smear, nucleic acid amplification with rifampin resistance, culture, molecular testing for isoniazid and fluoroquinolone resistance, and phenotypic susceptibility; an interferon-gamma release assay; HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C tests; and baseline blood count, liver and kidney tests, potassium, calcium, and magnesium
  • Infection control and public health: home airborne isolation with no students or visitors and a surgical mask around others; same-day report of suspected tuberculosis to the health department; a contact investigation of his students, friends, and other close contacts led by the health department
  • Nutrition: two dietitian visits in the first month, three meals and three energy-dense snacks a day, two oral nutrition supplement drinks a day, and weight at every visit
  • Support: plain information about how tuberculosis spreads, how quickly treatment makes him non-infectious, and that it is curable; help with what to tell his students; PHQ-9 at diagnosis, at two months, and at the end of treatment
  • Treatment: the four-month regimen of rifapentine 1200 mg, moxifloxacin 400 mg, isoniazid 300 mg, and pyrazinamide 1000 mg daily with food for eight weeks, then rifapentine, moxifloxacin, and isoniazid for nine weeks, with pyridoxine, by video-observed therapy seven days a week; complete when 119 doses are taken within five months
  • Monitoring: symptoms, weight, adverse effects (liver, tendons, nerves) and observed doses at every visit; liver tests at two to three weeks and for symptoms; sputum smears in the third week for release, then monthly culture until two are negative, including the two-month culture; phenotypic susceptibility including moxifloxacin; PHQ-9 at two months and at the end
  • Sweat chloride test and serum alpha-1 antitrypsin level once he is out of isolation, to address cystic fibrosis and alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency as the proposed alternatives

resource.title: Frédéric Chopin synthetic care plan
resource.description: Chronic cough with hemoptysis and weight loss in a 28-year-old pianist and piano teacher: chest X-ray and CT, three sputum samples for acid-fast smear, nucleic acid amplification, culture and drug susceptibility, an interferon-gamma release assay, HIV and hepatitis testing, home airborne isolation and same-day public-health reporting; the presenting problem resolved into a diagnosis of drug-susceptible cavitary pulmonary tuberculosis; an honest test of the proposed alternatives for his lifelong chest illness (sweat chloride for cystic fibrosis and a serum alpha-1 antitrypsin level), both normal; treatment with the four-month rifapentine, moxifloxacin, isoniazid, and pyrazinamide regimen by video-observed therapy under the 1834 CDC interim guidance and the ATS/CDC/IDSA guidelines, with eligibility, weight-band dosing, baseline and monitoring tests, and the 119-dose completion rule; release from isolation and return to teaching; a contact investigation led by the health department; care for moderate malnutrition; attention to low mood and the stigma he fears; and an honest record of a missed monthly symptom check.
